ceo.name: Anthony 'Tony' G. Capuano
ceo.background: Cornell Hotel Administration '87. Joined Marriott 1995 (after initial rejection) on Market Planning & Feasibility team. Rose through development roles: Western US/Canada full-service → North America/Caribbean/LatAm → Global Development (2009) → added Global Design (2014) → added Global Operations (Jan 2020). Pre-CEO title: Group President, Global Development, Design and Operations Services. Appointed CEO Feb 2021 following unexpected death of Arne Sorenson. Board member at McDonald's Corp, Economic Club of Washington DC, Save Venice.
ceo.track_record: Under his development leadership (2009-2020), Marriott grew from ~3,200 properties to 7,600+ properties and pipeline to 498,000 rooms (>50% international). Instrumental in 2016 Starwood Hotels acquisition. As CEO: signed record 1,200+ development deals in 2024 (~162K rooms), achieved 6.8% net rooms growth, expanded system to 9,600+ properties across 143 countries, grew Bonvoy to ~248M members. Stock has meaningfully outperformed S&P 500 during his tenure.

cfo.name: Kathleen 'Leeny' K. Oberg
cfo.background: BS Commerce (Finance & MIS) from UVA McIntire, MBA from Stanford GSB. Pre-Marriott: Chase Manhattan Bank, Goldman Sachs, Sallie Mae, Sodexo. Joined Marriott 1999 in Investor Relations. Held increasingly senior finance roles: SVP International Project Finance & Asset Management EMEA (London, 2006-2008), SVP Corporate & Development Finance (2008-2013), CFO of The Ritz-Carlton (2013-2015). CFO of Marriott International since Jan 1, 2016. Added EVP Development role in 2023. Adobe Board member. RETIRING effective March 31, 2026 — successor is Jen Mason (33-year Marriott veteran).

recent_changes.event: CFO Leeny Oberg announced retirement effective March 31, 2026. Jen Mason named successor CFO, Shawn Hill to lead Development.

Major continent leadership restructuring announced: Liam Brown (Group President US/Canada, ~40yr tenure) and Brian King (President Enterprise Transformation & CALA, ~30yr tenure) retiring end June 2026.
Satya Anand becomes Group President US/Canada/CALA; Neal Jones becomes President EMEA; Federico Greppi becomes President CALA. Jones and Anand join executive leadership team reporting to CEO Capuano.

insider_ownership_detail.note: Marriott family collectively holds very significant stake via direct and indirect/trust holdings. Figures overlap due to trust structures.

insider_ownership_detail.recent_activity: 17 insider transactions in Feb 2026 totaling $11.21M: 2 stock sales + 15 award grants (8 at $0). J.W. Marriott Jr. disposed ~$38K. Only sales in past 3 months — minimal and consistent with personal portfolio management, not bearish signaling.

compensation_highlights: CEO Capuano FY2024 total comp: $21.93M ($1.4M salary + $4.34M bonus + $3.88M options + $11.6M stock + $0.72M other). CEO salary unchanged; other NEO salaries increased ~4%. Annual cash incentive weighted 60% Adjusted EBITDA + 40% unifying goals. NEOs average 25+ years hospitality experience. Clawback/forfeiture provisions on equity awards. SARs (Stock Appreciation Rights) used with exercise price = grant-date average of high/low. Say-on-pay vote included in 2025 proxy.
governance_notes: Chairman: David S. Marriott (family member, since May 2022). Board committees: Audit, Nominating & Corporate Governance (NCGC), Human Resources & Compensation. Annual director elections (1-year terms), majority voting in uncontested elections. Strong ethics framework with Code of Ethics/Business Conduct Guide. Regular board meetings (min 4x/year). Long-tenured management culture — most senior executives have 25-40 year Marriott careers. Significant leadership transition underway in 2026 with CFO + two Group Presidents retiring simultaneously.
